answer.reason: The verses tell of Jonathan's own deeds and fate: his raid on the Philistines, his covenant with David, his rescue from Saul's oath, and his death at Gilboa.

clauses.english: attacked the Philistine garrison with his armourbearer, and the Philistines fled
clauses.quote: they fell before Jonathan; and his armourbearer slew after him.

clauses.english: made a covenant with David, loving him as his own soul
clauses.quote: Then Jonathan and David made a covenant, because he loved him as his own soul.

clauses.english: warned David of Saul's plan to kill him and pleaded for him with Saul
clauses.quote: Jonathan spake good of David unto Saul his father

clauses.english: was slain by the Philistines on mount Gilboa
clauses.quote: the Philistines slew Jonathan, and Abinadab, and Melchishua, Saul's sons.

doubts: 1SA 14:39-45 (Jonathan taken by lot for tasting honey and rescued by the people) could be a fifth clause; left out to keep the line short.
Genealogical verses (1CH 8:33-34, 1CH 9:39-40) and verses naming his son Mephibosheth only relate him to others, so were not used.
